title: Solar Panel Installation Issaquah WA — Permits, L&I Electrical, Roof Loads and PSE Net Metering
description: An Issaquah homeowner's guide to rooftop solar: when the City's solar checklist means no building permit, the L&I electrical permit and inspections, roof load and flashing rules, firefighter access pathways, shade from tall firs, and PSE interconnection and net metering.

search_intent: An Issaquah homeowner considering rooftop solar wants to know when a City building permit is required versus the exemption checklist, how the L&I electrical permit and inspections work, what roof load and flashing rules apply, how firefighter access pathways affect the layout, how shade from tall firs is evaluated, and how PSE interconnection and net metering work.
local_angles: City of Issaquah Solar Checklist (10/06/2025): most standard residential systems skip building permit if all items yes; still email checklist to Sustainability Team; L&I electrical always required
Load and height: 3.5 psf, 50 lb point load, 18 in max above roofing, not above ridge; flashing per IRC M2301.2.9; single-layer lightweight roof
MyBuildingPermit.com Tip Sheet 24: 36 in eave-to-ridge pathways, 18 in from ridge and from hips/valleys with panels both sides, 150 ft array limit
Issaquah electrical permits issued and inspected by L&I (Bellevue office); City business license still required; inspect before conceal and within 3 days of completion or 1 day of energizing

PSE Customer Connected Solar: application, Approval to Construct, install, electrical final, Notice of Completion, test/meters, approval to energize; Rate Schedule 150; credits expire March 31; 100 kW cap
Confirm City of Issaquah jurisdiction (Klahanie and Mirrormont are not); Permit Center 130 E Sunset Way, 425-837-3100; MyBuildingPermit.com
